behavior.arguments: rdi = 32-byte output pointer; rsi = 32-byte input pointer; rax is never written, so there is no return value determined by this window
behavior.copy_rule: for each of the eight 32-bit lanes, out lane = byte-reversed in lane: out[w*8..w*8+4] = reverse(in[w*8..w*8+4]) and out[w*8+4..w*8+8] = reverse(in[w*8+4..w*8+8]), for w in 0..3

edges.all_ff_input: out = 32 0xff bytes (byte reversal is the identity on uniform bytes)

behavior.formula: out = concat over w in 0..3 of (reverse(in[w*8..w*8+4]) ++ reverse(in[w*8+4..w*8+8]))
behavior.output_shape: 32 bytes written at (rdi); no return value; r8-r11 are caller-saved scratch
behavior.store_order_note: each bswapped word's low 32 bits are stored at out+4/+12/+20/+28 before its high 32 bits are stored at out+0/+8/+16/+24, but the final memory state is the per-lane byte reversal; no store in this window overwrites another

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, no runtime rebase

incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_slots_note: no relocation record of any type in .rela.dyn names this window as addend

scout_correction: the round-6 scout note described this window as a 32-bit-half swap (out word = in word rotated by 32 bits, out+0..3 = in[4..8]). The retained bytes show that is wrong: the low 32 bits of the bswapped word stored at out+4 are the byte-reversed second half, and the high 32 bits stored at out+0 are the byte-reversed first half. The correct rule is a per-32-bit-lane byte reversal with lanes in place, verified by two independent derivations (instruction-semantics emulation and lane-reversal restatement agree on all inputs, including the sequential edge)
